title: Optimizing Deep Learning Inference via Global Analysis and Tensor Expressions
problem: Existing DNN compilers cannot effectively exploit optimization opportunities across operator boundaries. As DNN complexity grows, optimization becomes increasingly difficult with limited inter-operator visibility.
motivation: Improving DNN inference performance is critical as neural network models grow in complexity and scale.
method: Souffle maps out how tensors (multi-dimensional data arrays) depend on each other by analyzing the math expressions that create them. It then breaks the large computation into smaller subprograms based on how data flows through the system and what hardware resources are available. Within each subprogram, it rearranges the operations to keep the math identical while letting more instructions run simultaneously, improving data reuse in the processor cache, and optimizing the overall execution schedule.
key_novelty: It optimizes across operators by mapping tensor dependencies through the entire program and splitting the work into subprograms based on this dataflow analysis.
contributions: Open-source compiler for cross-operator DNN inference optimization
Global tensor dependency graph representation using tensor expressions
Semantic-preserving transformations for instruction-level parallelism and data reuse optimization
primary_theme: Global compiler optimization for DNN inference
